"Hara Chana Masala Recipe" (Green Chickpea Curry) Ingredients:- Main Ingredients: * Fresh Green Chickpeas (Hara Chana): 2 cups (peeled and washed) * Cooking Oil: 4 tablespoons * Onion: ½ cup (finely chopped) * Fresh Coriander Leaves: A handful (finely chopped for garnish) * Water: 3 cups (or 1.5 glasses) For the Fresh Paste: * Tomatoes: 2 medium (chopped) * Ginger: 2-inch piece * Garlic: 10 to 12 cloves Whole Spices (Tadka): * Cumin Seeds (Jeera): 1 teaspoon * Bay Leaves (Tejpatta): 1 to 2 * Cinnamon Stick: 2-inch piece * Black Cardamom (Badi Elaichi): 1 (crushed) Ground Spices: * Turmeric Powder: ½ teaspoon * Kashmiri Red Chili Powder: 2 teaspoons * Coriander Powder: 1 teaspoon * Cumin Powder: ½ teaspoon * Garam Masala Powder: ½ teaspoon * Black Pepper Powder: ⅓ teaspoon * Salt: To taste Instructions:- 1. Prepare the Masala Paste: Place the chopped tomatoes, ginger, and garlic into a grinding jar. Blend into a smooth, fine paste without adding extra water. Set aside. 2. Sauté the Aromatics: Heat 4 tablespoons of oil in a pressure cooker over medium heat. Once hot, add the cumin seeds, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, and crushed black cardamom. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn golden brown. 3. Cook the Tomato Base: Add the freshly ground tomato-ginger-garlic paste to the onions. Stir well and cook for about 2 minutes. 4. Add Spices: Lower the heat and add the turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly and let the spices cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the oil starts to separate from the masala. You can add a splash of water (use the remains from the grinding jar) to prevent the spices from burning. 5. Sauté the Chickpeas: Add the 2 cups of fresh green chickpeas and salt to the cooker. Stir to coat the chickpeas in the masala and sauté for another 2 minutes. This allows the chickpeas to absorb the flavors. 6. Pressure Cook: Pour in 3 cups of water (adjust based on your preferred curry consistency). Close the lid of the pressure cooker. Cook on medium flame for 5 whistles. 7. Final Touch: Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally before opening the lid. Once open, add the fresh coriander leaves and mix gently. The curry will naturally thicken as it cools slightly. Serving Suggestion: Serve hot with roti, rice, or puris. For a "chaat-style" twist, garnish with chopped onions, tomatoes, green chilies, a sprinkle of roasted cumin powder, and some sev or bhujia.

"Masoor Dal (Red Lentil) Dosa Recipe" Ingredients:- For the Dosa Batter: * Masoor Dal (Red Lentils): 1 cup * Green Chilies: 2–3 (adjust to taste) * Garlic Cloves: 3–4 * Salt: To taste (approx. 1/2 tsp for grinding + 1/2 tsp for adjusting later) * Water: 1/2 cup (plus more if needed for consistency) * Cooking Oil: For frying For the Toppings (Optional): * Onion: 1 medium, finely chopped * Tomato: 1 small, finely chopped * Fresh Coriander: A handful, chopped * Peri-Peri Masala or Podi Masala: To sprinkle For the Green Chutney: * Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch * Garlic Cloves: 2–3 * Green Chilies: 2 * Lemon Juice: 1 tsp * Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia) or Sev: 1–2 tbsp (for thickness) * Salt: To taste * Water: As needed Preparation Steps:- 1. Prepare the Batter: * Wash 1 cup of Masoor Dal thoroughly. * Soak the dal in room temperature water for exactly 15 minutes. Note: Do not soak for longer, as the dal will become too soft and the dosa won't be crispy. * Drain the water and wash the dal 4–5 times under running water. * Transfer the soaked dal to a grinding jar. Add green chilies, garlic, salt, and 1/2 cup water. * Grind into a completely smooth paste. If the batter is too thick, add a little more water until it reaches a pouring consistency. * Transfer to a bowl and add another 1/2 tsp of salt (adjust to taste). Mix well. 2. Prepare the Green Chutney: * In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal (or sev), and salt. * Add a splash of water and blend until smooth. Set aside. 3. Cook the Dosa: * Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over low-medium heat. * Lightly grease the tawa with a drop of oil and then wipe it off completely with a tissue paper. The surface should not be greasy. * Pour a ladleful of batter into the center of the tawa. Using the back of the spoon, spread it in a circular motion moving outwards. * For Veggie Dosa: Sprinkle chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander, and peri-peri masala on top while the batter is still slightly wet. * Drizzle a little oil around the edges and on top. * Cook on low-medium heat for about 3 minutes. Be patient; Masoor dal takes a bit longer to crisp up than rice dosa. * Flip (Optional): If you prefer it cooked on both sides like an Uttapam, flip and cook for 30 seconds. For a classic crispy dosa, cook on one side only until the base is golden brown and firm. 4. Serving: * Fold the dosa and serve hot with the prepared green chutney. 👍

*"Gluten-free Jowar Chocolate Appe Cake (also known as Choco Balls)"* This is a healthy and perfect snack for kids' tiffins. It’s prepared in an appe pan (aebleskiver pan) in just 10 minutes without an oven or air fryer. *_Ingredients:-_* * Jowar Flour (Sorghum): 1 cup (Can substitute with Ragi or Bajra flour) * Powdered Sugar or Jaggery Powder: ½ cup * Cocoa Powder: ¼ cup * Milk Powder: ¼ cup (Adds richness) * Baking Powder: 1 tsp * Baking Soda: ½ tsp * Vanilla Essence: A few drops * Ghee or Oil: 2 tbsp * Milk: 1 cup (Room temperature) * Additional Ghee/Oil: For greasing and flipping *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Batter* * In a large mixing bowl, combine the jowar flour, powdered sugar (or jaggery), cocoa powder, milk powder, baking powder, and baking soda. * Add the vanilla essence and 2 tablespoons of ghee (or oil). Mix these ingredients well. * Gradually pour in the milk. Use about half first, then the rest, whisking until you achieve a smooth, thick batter. *2. Preheat and Grease* * Place an appe pan on the stove over low heat. * Lightly grease each mold with a little bit of ghee or oil. *3. Cook the Choco Balls* * Give the batter a quick stir. Fill each mold only halfway with the batter. Do not overfill, as the cakes will rise and double in size. * Cover the pan with a lid and cook on low flame for about 4 minutes. * Once the tops look set and the balls have puffed up, apply a tiny amount of ghee on top of each ball. *4. Flip and Finish* * Using a wooden stick or a small spoon, carefully flip each ball over. * Cook the other side for another 3 minutes on low flame. Do not cover the pan during this second stage to prevent steam from making the cakes soggy. *5. Serving* * Once cooked through, remove the choco balls from the pan. * *Serve* them warm or at room temperature. They pair perfectly with chocolate sauce, Nutella, or can be enjoyed plain as a healthy treat.

*"Recipe: Crispy Veg Cutlets"* *_Ingredients:-_* *For the Vegetable Mixture:* * Boiled Potatoes: 4 medium (peeled and mashed) * Paneer: ½ cup (grated) * Carrots: ½ cup (grated) * Capsicum: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Onion: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Green Chilies: 1 tbsp (finely chopped) * Coriander Leaves: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Chili Flakes: 1 tsp * Mixed Herbs / Oregano: 1 tsp * Black Pepper Powder: 1/3 tsp * Lemon Juice: 1 tbsp (can substitute with Amchur or Chaat Masala) * Salt: To taste * (Optional: You can also add finely chopped cabbage, beans, or spinach) *For the Slurry (Coating):* * Corn Flour: 4 tbsp * All-Purpose Flour (Maida): 4 tbsp * Black Pepper Powder: A pinch * Salt: A pinch * Water: As needed to make a thick batter *For the Outer Layer:* * Bread Crumbs: As required * Oil: For deep frying *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Vegetable Base* In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, grated paneer, carrots, capsicum, onions, green chilies, and coriander leaves. Add the chili flakes, mixed herbs, black pepper powder, salt, and lemon juice. Mix everything thoroughly by hand, ensuring the potatoes are well mashed and the spices are evenly distributed. *2. Shape the Cutlets* Clean your hands and take a small portion of the mixture. Roll it between your palms and shape it as desired. You can make them oval, egg-shaped, or the traditional round flat shape. Repeat until all the mixture is used. *3. Prepare the Coating Slurry* In a separate bowl, mix equal parts corn flour and maida (4 tbsp each). Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Gradually add water and whisk until you achieve a smooth, thick batter. Ensure it is not too thin. *4. Coat the Cutlets* Place the bread crumbs in a plate. Take a shaped cutlet and dip it into the flour slurry using a fork (this helps drain the excess batter). Immediately place it onto the bread crumbs and coat it evenly on all sides, tapping gently to ensure the crumbs stick. * Pro Tip: For extra crispiness and to prevent the cutlet from breaking in oil, you can do a "Double Coating" by dipping the bread-crumbed cutlet back into the slurry and then into the bread crumbs a second time. *5. Fry the Cutlets* Heat oil in a pan on medium to medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, carefully place the cutlets in the pan. Avoid low heat as it will make the cutlets soggy; high heat ensures they turn crispy. Fry until they reach a dark golden brown color, flipping them occasionally to ensure even cooking. *6. Serving* Remove the cutlets and place them on a kitchen paper towel to drain any excess oil. Serve these hot and crispy veg cutlets with tomato ketchup or green chutney. Note: You can store these prepared, uncooked cutlets in an airtight container in the freezer. When ready to eat, take them out an hour before and deep fry or air fry them directly.

*"Restaurant-style Veg Burrito Bowl Recipe"* *_Ingredients:-_* *For the Paneer:* * Paneer: 200g (cut into large cubes) * Butter: 1 tsp * Chilli Flakes: 1 tsp * Oregano/Mixed Herbs: 1 tsp * Salt: To taste *For the Rajma (Beans):* * Boiled Rajma (Kidney Beans): 1/2 cup * Garlic: 1 tsp (finely chopped) * Onion: 4 tbsp (finely chopped) * Tomato: 4 tbsp (finely chopped) * Schezwan Chutney: 1 tsp * Cooking Oil: 1 tbsp * Salt: To taste * Water: As needed *For the Cilantro Lime Rice:* * Cooked Rice: 1 cup (preferably sticky variety like Indrayani or Govind Bhog) * Butter: 1 tbsp * Coriander Leaves: A handful (finely chopped) * Lemon Juice: From half a lemon * Salt: To taste *For the Sautéed Salad:* * Onion: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Yellow Capsicum: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Red Capsicum: 2 tbsp (sliced lengthwise) * Boiled Corn: 2 tbsp * Mixed Herbs: 1/2 tsp * Chilli Flakes: 1/2 tsp * Cooking Oil: 1 tsp * Salt: To taste *For the Yogurt Dressing:* * Greek Yogurt: 1/2 cup (or thick hung curd) * Garlic: 4 cloves (grated) * Black Pepper: 1/5 tsp * Coriander/Mint Leaves: Finely chopped * Salt: To taste *Additional Toppings:* * Avocado: 1 (sliced or mashed into guacamole) * Cherry Tomatoes: Handful (halved) * Lemon Juice & Salt: For seasoning the tomatoes * Tortilla Chips/Nachos: For crunch *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Paneer* Heat 1 tsp butter in a pan. Add 200g paneer cubes. Season with 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp oregano, and salt. Sauté on medium flame for about a minute until lightly golden. Avoid overcooking to keep the paneer soft. Remove and set aside. *2. Cook the Rajma* In the same pan, heat 1 tbsp oil. Add 1 tsp chopped garlic, 4 tbsp onions, and 4 tbsp tomatoes. Sauté until soft. Add 1/2 cup boiled rajma, salt, and 1 tsp Schezwan chutney for a zingy flavor. Add a little water and cook on low flame for 5 minutes. Mash a few beans with a masher for a thick texture, then dry out the excess moisture. Set aside. *3. Make Cilantro Lime Rice* Heat 1 tbsp butter in a pan. Add 1 cup cooked rice, salt, and plenty of fresh coriander leaves. Toss for 10 seconds to infuse the flavor. Turn off the heat and squeeze in lemon juice. Mix well and set aside. *4. Sauté the Salad* Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan. Add sliced onions, red and yellow capsicums, and boiled corn. Season with 1/2 tsp mixed herbs, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes, and salt. Sauté quickly just to remove the rawness while keeping the crunch. Set aside. *5. Prepare the Dressing & Extras* * Dressing: Mix 1/2 cup Greek yogurt with 4 grated garlic cloves, black pepper, salt, and chopped coriander. * Tomato Salad: Toss halved cherry tomatoes with a little salt and lemon juice. * Avocado: Slice one fresh avocado or mash it with onions and lime to make guacamole. Assembling the Burrito Bowl * Rice Base: Press the Cilantro Lime Rice into a small bowl and flip it onto the center of your serving plate/bowl. * Arrange Sides: Place the sautéed paneer, rajma, sautéed salad, cherry tomato salad, and avocado slices in sections around the rice. * Final Touch: Add a generous dollop of the garlic yogurt dressing. * Garnish: Serve with a side of tortilla chips or nachos for crunch and a lemon wedge. *Enjoy* your homemade, healthy, and vibrant Veg Burrito Bowl! 👍

Because the extracted mango juice was quite thin, women added dahi (yogurt) and besan (chickpea flour) to thicken it. This created a sweet, sour, and savory mango-based kadh I. Zero water

You guys do not need to constantly prove how funny or entertaining you are, everyone already knows that and loves you for it. Your punches and reactions are great, but the guest should ideally have the highest talking time in their own episode.

No offense at all, just genuine feedback from someone who truly enjoys watching Lavari and wants the conversations to feel even better. Keep doing amazing work.

Interestingly, the origin of 'cheers' is often linked to a tradition from centuries ago when kings and nobles invited one another to feasts. As a gesture of trust and courtesy, they would clink their glasses together, causing a small amount of each drink to spill into the other person's cup. This symbolized that neither drink had been poisoned, since both parties would be drinking the same mixture. Over time, this act became a sign of goodwill and friendship, which is why we still say 'cheers' before taking a drink today.

Spicy Matar (Green Peas) Sandwich Recipe ​Ingredients:- ​For the Pea Filling: ​Fresh Green Peas: 1 cup (Fresh is preferred over frozen for better texture and flavor) ​Garlic: 3–4 cloves ​Green Chilies: 2 (adjust to spice preference) ​Oil: 1 teaspoon ​Salt: To taste ​For the Spicy Green Chutney: ​Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch ​Garlic: 2–3 cloves ​Green Chilies: 1–2 ​Lemon Juice: 1 tablespoon ​Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia): 1 tablespoon (or Sev Bhujia for thickness) ​Salt: To taste ​Water: A splash for grinding ​For Assembly: ​Bread Slices: 4 slices (White, Brown, or Sourdough) ​Cheese Slices: 2 slices ​Butter: For toasting ​Instructions:- ​1. Prepare the Pea Filling: ​Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a pan over medium flame. ​Add the garlic cloves and green chilies. ​Add the fresh green peas and a pinch of salt. ​Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until the raw smell disappears. Do not overcook them; they should just be soft enough to grind. ​Remove from heat and let the mixture cool completely. ​Once cooled, transfer to a grinder and pulse a few times to get a coarse, grainy texture. Avoid making a smooth paste. ​2. Make the Green Chutney: ​In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal, salt, and a little water. ​Blend into a thick, spicy chutney. ​3. Assemble the Sandwich: ​Take two slices of bread. Apply a generous, thick layer of the coarse pea mixture on both slices. ​Place a cheese slice on top of the pea filling on one of the bread slices. This helps balance the spiciness of the peas and chutney. ​On two separate bread slices (the "top" slices), spread a layer of the spicy green chutney. ​Close the sandwiches by placing the chutney-spread bread over the cheese and pea-covered bread. ​4. Toast to Perfection: ​Heat a tawa (griddle) over low flame to ensure the sandwich gets extra crispy. ​Spread some butter on the tawa and place the sandwiches on it. ​Press gently and cook until the bottom is golden brown. ​Apply butter on the top side of the bread before flipping. ​Flip carefully and toast the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes until both sides are golden brown and the cheese inside has melted. ​5. Serving: ​Cut the sandwiches diagonally. * ​Serve hot with tomato ketchup and a side of potato chips for a cafe-style experience. 👍
